response.justification: The candidate clearly exceeds the technical bar: ~15 years of software development across web, mobile, desktop and embedded, plus genuine developer-tooling depth (authored a D test runner and assertion library, built CI/CD and device-orchestration infrastructure, MCP code generators, IDE components at National Instruments). However, the resume shows no evidence of the core requirement for this role — formal people management. There are no manager titles, no mention of direct reports, performance reviews, 1:1s, headcount, or leading organizational change; 'Founder' of a small OSS project and 'Staff Engineer' are individual-contributor/technical-lead signals at best. Mobile-platform exposure is real but dated and limited (iOS/tvOS apps in 2015-16). Worth a screening call to probe for unlisted leadership scope, but as written this is a strong senior IC profile applied to a Level II manager opening.
strengths: Deep, demonstrable developer-tooling and test-infrastructure work (Trial, Fluent-Asserts, CI/CD, IDE components)
15+ years of broad hands-on engineering — comfortably exceeds the 8-year minimum and supports hands-on coding/code review duties
Strong mentoring and knowledge-sharing track record: multi-module Selenium course, full-day workshops, conference talks
concerns: No documented people-management experience — misses the 2-year minimum and the role's core focus
No evidence of roadmap ownership, performance management, or leading organizational change
Mobile-platform experience is thin and roughly a decade old; no Master's/PhD for the preferred profile

key_factors.factor: Developer tools and testing infrastructure depth
